metadata.name: cairn
metadata.description: cairn is the page you hand to the people you host services for: family, a club, whoever ends up using your server. One YAML file in, a static multilingual directory out, with no account to create, no database and no outbound requests. It shows your services and nothing else: no widgets, no Docker socket, no metrics. Each service can show a live status pill pulled from Gatus or Uptime Kuma, so visitors see what is up before they click, and cairn serves its own legal and privacy pages. It ships as a single static Go binary in a FROM scratch image, around 4 MB to pull, and it writes nothing at runtime, so it runs read-only with every Linux capability dropped.
metadata.tagline: The directory page for the people you host services for
metadata.author: MorganKryze

volumes.description: The YAML files that describe your services; cairn only ever reads this folder

before_install.en_us:
cairn needs no environment variable and no secret to run: it reads YAML files from the folder mounted at /config, so there is nothing to fill in here.
The first run works with that folder empty, because cairn then serves a getting-started page instead of failing. To list your own services, put a services.yaml in the host folder mapped to /config, which on CasaOS is /DATA/AppData/cairn/config. cairn picks the file up within seconds, with no restart, and if the file is invalid it keeps the previous configuration and logs the key it did not recognise.
Full reference: https://github.com/MorganKryze/cairn/tree/main/docs

after_install.en_us:
Open cairn at the address your platform shows for it: host port 8080 on most platforms, 18080 on Umbrel. With an empty config folder cairn serves a getting-started page instead of failing, so the first run always works.

Create a services.yaml in cairn's config folder and cairn picks it up within seconds, with no restart. Where that folder is depends on the platform: CasaOS uses /DATA/AppData/cairn/config, Runtipi and Umbrel use cairn/config under the app data directory, and on Portainer, Dockge and Cosmos it is the Docker volume big-bear-cairn_config, so either write the file there or point the /config mount at a directory of your own.

If a file is invalid, cairn keeps the previous configuration and logs which key it did not recognise, so a typo never takes the page down. Full reference: https://github.com/MorganKryze/cairn/tree/main/docs
